newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD - Markets eye host of European events.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Markets eye host of European events.

text.p: Political developments in Britain and France, speculation over Italian interest rates, sentiment on European monetary union, and German M3 data will dominate markets this week, analysts said.

The U.S. and Japan have relatively light weeks in terms of data but with dollar/yen moving fast and talk of political pressure on Japanese interest rates, authorities' comments in both countries will be under scrutiny, they added.
For Paul Horne, chief international economist at Smith Barney in Paris, the main event was clear -- "Mr Chirac's decision on whether to call early elections."
There has been speculation French President Jacques Chirac will call early elections, speculation which his office has allowed to rumble for days.
Analysts said Chirac may want to capitalise on a slightly better economic outlook and at the same time renew the government's mandate for European Economic and Monetary union (EMU).
The French education minister, commenting on widespread rumours of the election being brought forward from March 1998, has said the president could announce a decision on Thursday.
"A decision not to hold early elections would allow French voters to be polarised around Europe," Horne said. But if a ballot were called, he said surveys suggest the centre-right could win.
While French markets have been roiled by the new political uncertainty, Britain is winding up a long election campaign.
This week will be the last full week of campaigning before a general election on May 1, one in which opinion surveys overwhelmingly favour the opposition Labour party to win.
Britain has several key economic reports, with retail sales for March and a Confederation of British industry report on Wednesday, and gross domestic product numbers on Friday.
In Italy, there has been continued speculation that Italian interest rates will fall.
"There's a small possibility of a rate cut next week," said Mark Fox, chief European strategist for fixed income at Lehman Brothers in London.
Horne at Smith Barney said a rate cut was likely. "Spain did it, Italy can do it too,"
From a data point of view, the main event will be German M3 figures, analysts said.

"Bundesbank chief economist (Otmar) Issing has already flagged the likelihood of a slowdown in the headline number, but watch out for another strong lending figure," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International here.

A Reuters survey of economists on average predicted annualised seasonally adjusted M3 growth in March, due early in the week ahead, would be 8.3 percent. That compared with February's 9.1 percent. Issing on Thursday said he expected M3 to have slowed in March.
In the U.S. the only data of note are import and export prices on Tuesday and existing homes on Friday.

Meanwhile, after a flurry of comments from Japanese authorities, the market is speculating again about a possible increase in the 0.50 percent official discount rate. "It's possible the MOF will hit the ODR for 25, possibly 50 basis points in the next few weeks," Horne said.
